notes.decision: Translated 'labor' as Lyc reduction of ⲣ̄-ϩⲓⲥⲉ 'do toil/labor.' Context (alongside wage-laborers in the world to receive money) requires a labor-verb. Alternative reading as Lyc form of ⲣⲟⲉⲓⲥ 'be vigilant/watchful' is possible but contextually less apt.

Tentative 'wage-laborers'; agent-noun ⲣⲉϩ-/ⲣⲉϥ- + unidentified ⲕⲗⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ. Possibly Greek-derived (κλωνεύω 'turn,' κλόνος 'tumult,' or κοινωνός 'partner'). The context of going-around-for-wages suggests itinerant workers/laborers.

Read as Lycopolitan negative habitual 3pl/impersonal 'they do not give / it is not given,' with ⲙⲁϩ- corresponding to Sahidic ⲙⲉⲩ-. The clause 'this is therefore why no apocalypse is given to the elect' fits the contrastive logic with line 5 'but the matter is hidden from them indeed until...'

Parsed as Lycopolitan conjunctive ⲛ̄(ϥ)ⲧⲉⲟⲩⲟ-ⲥ 'and he proclaims/declares her,' coordinating with the preceding ϣⲁⲣⲉ ⲡⲉⲕⲗⲉⲕⲧⲟⲥ ⲧⲁϣⲉⲁⲓϣ ⲙⲙⲁⲥ. The verb ⲧⲉⲟⲩⲟ 'declare' is in glossary; the suffixed form ⲧⲉⲟⲩⲁⲥ 'declare her' is also attested. Lyc ⲛϩ- for conjunctive ⲛϥ- is regular.
The ordinal series ⲧⲧⲙⲁϩⲥⲛⲉⲩ 'second,' ⲧⲧⲙⲁϩϣⲁⲙⲧ 'third,' [ⲧⲧⲙⲁϩϩⲧⲁⲩ] 'fourth,' [ⲧⲧⲙⲁϩϯⲟⲩ] 'fifth' enumerates the Mind of Light's five works. The first (ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ) is Wisdom; the second is faith (ⲛⲁϩⲧⲉ).

Translated 'patience of the privation in secret.' ⲧϩⲣⲡⲧⲉ as Lyc reflex of ϩⲣⲟϣ-ϩⲏⲧ / ϩⲣⲏⲧⲉ 'patience, long-suffering.' ⲡϣⲱⲱⲧ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ literally 'the cutting forth' = lack/deficiency/privation in ascetic register — the privation the elect bears patiently while the world's people do not perceive it. ⲛϩⲉⲡⲡ = 'in secret' (from ϩⲱⲡ 'hide').

Habitual ϣⲁϩ- + ϣⲁⲁⲧ qualitative of ϣⲱⲱⲧ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'be cut off, be deficient, suffer want.' The elect is habitually 'cut off' (in the sense of lacking) among those without the hope of God — captures the Manichaean ascetic motif of patient endurance of want.

The numeral ⲣ̄ⲅ = 103 functions as chapter-number marker. Its triple appearance (lines 8, 10 [twice]) reflects the standard Kephalaia heading layout where the chapter number flanks the title. Translated as plain numeral '103.'

Tentative 'These belong to every man.' Parsed as ⲛⲉⲓ̈ ('these' demonstrative) + ⲉⲧϩ (Lyc qualitative possibly of ⲱⲡ 'be reckoned/belong') + ⲛ̄-ⲟⲩⲁⲛ-ⲛⲓⲙ ('to every-one'). Alternative: ⲛⲉⲓ̈ⲉⲧϩ as locative 'unto him' yielding 'these are unto everyone.' The leer indicates a section break; this phrase opens a new statement.
